correctedCritiques.con-objective-logic-subjective-reasoning: Strongest feature: The reply preserves objective logical constraints while distinguishing valid inferential relations from conclusions conditioned by adopted premises, offering a coherent compatibility answer instead of denying reasoning’s normative architecture. Principal limitation: Describing reason itself as subjective conflates discretionary premise selection with inferential validity, creating terminological instability and obscuring whether subjectivity concerns psychology, justification, or logical consequence. Live burden: Con must formulate this distinction, explain why objective validity requires no divine ontology, and demonstrate how premise-relative moral conclusions differ from categorical obligations without collapsing either category. Locked score: Strong band recognizes direct engagement, coherent structure, scope stability, and proportionate possibility language, while the ambiguous account of reason and incomplete ontology of norms prevent resolution of the grounding challenge.
correctedCritiques.pro-evolution-self-reference-basic-belie: Strongest feature: The reply identifies a genuine self-referential problem for comprehensive evolutionary debunking and contrasts an unavoidable assumption with the epistemologically richer category of properly basic belief. Principal limitation: It expands the opponent’s causal explanation into claiming every thought is evolution-produced, presumes causation defeats justification, and invokes proper basicality without specifying reliability, defeasibility, or warrant conditions. Live burden: Pro must establish why evolved mechanisms cannot track truth, explain why correction cannot escape the defeater, and show why moral conviction qualifies as basic while evolutionary belief receives no comparable entitlement. Locked score: The mixed band reflects diagnostic relevance and recoverable challenge but recognizes overstated necessity, unstable scope and terminology, missing qualification, and inadequate support for self-defeat claim and epistemic asymmetry.
